abstract: Centrioles are microtubule-based organelles that exhibit a highly conserved architecture that is essential for their function. However, the molecular mechanisms maintaining their structural integrity remain incompletely understood. Here, we characterize CCDC81 as a conserved microtubule-binding protein that contributes to centriole organization. Using expansion microscopy, we localize CCDC81 to the A-C linker of Chlamydomonas basal bodies, where it associates with POC11, the homolog of human A-C linker protein CCDC77. We demonstrate that CCDC81 directly binds microtubules through its N-terminal HU domains, promotes microtubule bundling, and stabilizes microtubules by reducing depolymerization and increasing rescue frequency. Cryo-electron microscopy further reveals its association with the outer microtubule lattice. We identify distinct domains mediating CCDC81 interaction with POC11 and propose a molecular organization of this complex within the A-C linker. Importantly, CCDC81 also localizes to human centrioles, where its depletion disrupts centriole architecture and A-C linker organization, with defects exacerbated by co-depletion of CCDC77. Together, our findings establish CCDC81 as a conserved regulator of microtubule organization and centriole structural integrity.
